verses.text: You foolish Galatians! Who put a spell on you? Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed to you as crucified.
Tell me this: Did you receive the Spirit by doing what the law requires, or by hearing and believing?
Are you really this foolish? You began by the Spirit—are you now trying to finish by human effort?
Did you go through so much for nothing? Was it really for nothing?
Does God give you the Spirit and work miracles among you because you do what the law requires, or because you hear and believe?
In the same way, Abraham ‘believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.’
So understand this: those who have faith are Abraham's children.
Scripture foresaw that God would make the Gentiles right through faith, and announced the Good News to Abraham in advance: ‘All nations will be blessed through you.’
So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
Everyone who relies on doing what the law requires is under a curse. Scripture says, ‘Cursed is everyone who doesn't keep doing everything written in the book of the law.’
It's clear that no one is made right with God through the law, because Scripture says, ‘The righteous will live by faith.’
But the law isn't based on faith. It says, ‘The one who does these things will live by them.’
Christ rescued us from the law's curse by becoming a curse for us. Scripture says, ‘Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.’
He did this so Abraham's blessing could reach the Gentiles through Christ Jesus, and so that through faith we could receive the promised Spirit.
Brothers and sisters, let me use a human example: once a person's covenant is confirmed, no one can cancel it or add conditions to it.
The promises were made to Abraham and his descendant. Scripture doesn't say ‘to descendants,’ as if it meant many, but ‘to your descendant’—meaning Christ.
Here's what I mean: the law, which came 430 years later, doesn't cancel the covenant God had already confirmed, or nullify the promise.
If the inheritance came through the law, it wouldn't come through a promise. But God freely gave it to Abraham by promise.
So why was the law given? It was added because of wrongdoing, until the descendant came to whom the promise was made. Angels delivered it through a mediator.
But a mediator represents more than one party, while God is one.
So is the law against God's promises? Absolutely not! If a law had been given that could make people alive, then righteousness would indeed come through the law.
But Scripture has locked everything under sin, so that the promise through faith in Jesus Christ could be given to those who believe.
Before faith came, the law kept us in custody, locked up until the faith that was coming would be revealed.
So the law became our guardian until Christ came, so we could be made right through faith.
But now that faith has come, we're no longer under a guardian.
Through faith in Christ Jesus, you are all God's children.
All of you who were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
There is no Jew or Greek, slave or free, male and female. You are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's descendants and heirs according to the promise.
